summary.text: Bony fish, or Osteichthyes, are vertebrates whose skeletons are mostly made of bone, and about 28,000 species are alive today.
They split into ray-finned fish, which make up most living fish, and lobe-finned fish, which gave rise to all land vertebrates.
Early bony fish had gut outpouches for breathing air; in ray-finned fish these became swim bladders, and in the line leading to land animals they became lungs.

facts.label: Oldest fossils
facts.value: About 436 million years old, from the early Silurian

facts.label: Gill covers
facts.value: A pair of opercula draw water across the gills

facts.label: Body temperature
facts.value: Mostly cold-blooded; tuna and swordfish evolved warmth

items.prompt: A bony fish rests motionless on the bottom yet keeps breathing. How does it keep water moving past its gills?

options.label: It gulps air at the surface every few seconds
Its scales, set under the skin, absorb oxygen directly
Its gill covers can actively draw water across the gills
Its cartilage plates pump water as the fish drifts

items.explain: Bony fish evolved a pair of opercula that actively draw water across the gills, so they can breathe without swimming.

items.prompt: Your lungs and a ray-finned fish's buoyancy organ do different jobs. What do they share?

options.label: Both grew out of the same early gut pouches used to breathe air
Both began as scale-covered sacs near the skin
Both formed from the gill covers of early fish
Both came from the bones of the fins

items.explain: Early bony fish had respiratory outpouches beside the gullet; in ray-finned fish they became swim bladders and in the line to land vertebrates they became lungs.

items.prompt: Some current papers place mammals inside the "bony fish" group. What is their reasoning?

options.label: Mammals keep a swim bladder alongside their lungs
Mammals have skeletons made mainly of soft cartilage
Mammal skin carries the same three kinds of scales
Land animals descend from lobe-finned fish, so they sit inside the group

items.explain: Since 2013 papers treat Osteichthyes as a clade that includes tetrapods, which evolved from lobe-finned fish.

items.prompt: A paleontologist traces the ancestors of the first land-walking vertebrates. Which bony fish group does she follow?

options.label: Ray-finned fish
Lobe-finned fish
Cartilaginous fish
Acanthodians

items.explain: The lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) gave rise to all land vertebrates, as their paired fins developed jointed skeletons that became limbs.

items.prompt: Most bony fish take on the temperature of the water around them. How can a swordfish stay warmer?

options.label: Some large ocean fish separately evolved varying degrees of internal heat
Its thick bony scales trap heat from the sun
It stays in shallow water where warmth collects
It breathes air through lungs, which warms it

items.explain: Bony fish are primitively cold-blooded, but larger marine species such as the opah, swordfish and tuna independently evolved various levels of endothermy.

items.prompt: Cosmoid, ganoid and teleost scales look different under a microscope. What do all three share?

options.label: Each is topped with a layer of enamel
Each has a layer of dentin in its middle
Each grows from a base of bone
Each pokes up through the skin's outer layer

items.explain: All the scale types have a base of bone; ganoid and cosmoid scales add enamel, cosmoid adds dentin, and none penetrate the epidermis.
